This notebook demonstrates the most powerful feature of Novel Entity Matcher — the
**discovery pipeline**. It doesn't just reject unknown inputs, it discovers what they are
by clustering novel samples and proposing new class names.

## Setup: Product Categories

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| cache: true
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from novelentitymatcher import Matcher, NovelEntityMatcher
from novelentitymatcher.novelty import DetectionConfig
from novelentitymatcher.novelty.config.strategies import ConfidenceConfig, KNNConfig

entities = [
    {"id": "electronics", "name": "Electronics"},
    {"id": "clothing", "name": "Clothing"},
    {"id": "food", "name": "Food & Beverage"},
    {"id": "books", "name": "Books & Media"},
    {"id": "sports", "name": "Sports Equipment"},
]

training_texts = [
    "smartphone case", "laptop charger", "wireless headphones",
    "tablet screen protector", "USB-C cable",
    "winter jacket", "running shoes", "cotton t-shirt",
    "wool sweater", "leather belt",
    "organic coffee beans", "dark chocolate bar", "sparkling water",
    "olive oil", "protein bars",
    "science fiction novel", "cookbook recipes", "children's picture book",
    "history biography", "self-help guide",
    "yoga mat", "tennis racket", "swimming goggles",
    "dumbbell set", "hiking backpack",
]

training_labels = [
    "electronics", "electronics", "electronics", "electronics", "electronics",
    "clothing", "clothing", "clothing", "clothing", "clothing",
    "food", "food", "food", "food", "food",
    "books", "books", "books", "books", "books",
    "sports", "sports", "sports", "sports", "sports",
]

matcher = Matcher(entities=entities, model="minilm", threshold=0.6)
matcher.fit(texts=training_texts, labels=training_labels)
```

## Stage 1–2: Match + Detect

```{python}
#| label: queries
#| cache: true
queries = [
    "bluetooth speaker", "denim jeans", "green tea",
    "mystery thriller", "basketball hoop",
    "bitcoin hardware wallet", "smart thermostat", "electric scooter",
    "music streaming subscription", "robot vacuum cleaner",
    "3D printer filament", "drone camera",
    "solar panel kit", "meditation app", "board game expansion",
]

nm = NovelEntityMatcher(
    matcher=matcher,
    detection_config=DetectionConfig(
        strategies=["confidence", "knn_distance"],
        confidence=ConfidenceConfig(threshold=0.45),
        knn_distance=KNNConfig(k=20, distance_threshold=0.45),
        combine_method="weighted",
    ),
)

rows = []
for q in queries:
    r = nm.match(q)
    rows.append({
        "query": q,
        "is_novel": r.is_novel,
        "matched": r.predicted_id if not r.is_novel else "—",
        "confidence": f"{r.score:.2%}",
        "novel_score": f"{r.novel_score:.3f}" if r.novel_score else "—",
    })

pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

The first 5 queries match known categories. The remaining 10 are from **emerging categories**
the matcher has never seen — cryptocurrency hardware, smart home devices, electric vehicles,
streaming services, IoT devices, and more.

## Stage 3–5: Full Discovery

```{python}
#| label: discovery
#| cache: true
report = nm.discover_novel_classes(
    queries, run_llm_proposal=False, return_metadata=True
)

novel = report.novel_sample_report.novel_samples
print(f"Novel samples detected: {len(novel)} / {len(queries)}")
print(f"Clusters found: {len(report.discovery_clusters)}")

novel_rows = []
for s in novel:
    novel_rows.append({
        "text": s.text,
        "predicted_class": s.predicted_class,
        "confidence": f"{s.confidence:.2%}",
        "novelty_score": f"{s.novelty_score:.3f}" if s.novelty_score else "—",
        "cluster_id": s.cluster_id if s.cluster_id is not None else "unclustered",
    })

pd.DataFrame(novel_rows)
```

```{python}
#| label: cluster-chart
#| cache: true
clusters = report.discovery_clusters
if clusters:
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
    ids = [f"Cluster {c.cluster_id}" for c in clusters]
    sizes = [c.sample_count for c in clusters]
    colors = ["#3498db", "#2ecc71", "#e74c3c", "#f39c12", "#9b59b6", "#1abc9c"]
    ax.barh(range(len(ids)), sizes, color=colors[:len(ids)])
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(ids)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(ids)
    ax.set_xlabel("Sample Count")
    ax.set_title("Novel Sample Clusters")
    for i, s in enumerate(sizes):
        ax.text(s + 0.1, i, str(s), va="center", fontweight="bold")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("No clusters found (novel samples may be too diverse or too few).")
```

## Cluster Evidence

```{python}
#| label: evidence
#| cache: true
if clusters:
    evidence_rows = []
    for c in clusters:
        ev = c.evidence
        keywords = (ev.keywords if ev else c.keywords)[:8]
        examples = (ev.representative_examples if ev else c.example_texts)[:3]
        evidence_rows.append({
            "cluster": f"Cluster {c.cluster_id}",
            "size": c.sample_count,
            "keywords": ", ".join(keywords),
            "examples": "; ".join(examples),
        })
    pd.DataFrame(evidence_rows)
else:
    print("No clusters to analyze.")
```

**Key insight:** The discovery pipeline automatically groups novel inputs into coherent clusters and extracts keywords. In production, an LLM would propose class names for each cluster — this is skipped here (no API key required). Use `run_llm_proposal=True` with an LLM provider for full proposals.

## Production Usage

```python
from novelentitymatcher import DiscoveryPipeline

pipeline = DiscoveryPipeline(
    entities=entities,
    model="minilm",
    novelty_strategy="knn_distance",
    min_cluster_size=3,
)
pipeline.fit(texts=training_texts, labels=training_labels)

# For async: report = await pipeline.discover(queries)
# For sync: use NovelEntityMatcher.discover_novel_classes() instead
```
